title: Hints of a Population of Solar System Analog Planets from ALMA
question: Does the compact disk around GQ Lup A show DSHARP-like substructures (gaps/rings), and what planet masses would they imply?

what.value: Total dust mass 5.9 Earth masses, r_in=1.5 au, r_out=23.8 au, gamma=0.1 (Model A)

evidence.quote: we begin with a total dust mass of 5.9$M_{\Earth}$ from Model A in (cite: Wu_2017), one of their best-fit models.

what.value: Lower total gas mass from simple parametric disk model

evidence.quote: We also use a second, lower value of total gas mass that (cite: MacGregor_2017) retrieved using a simple parametric model of disk structure.

evidence.loc: Deriving the surface brightness profile of the 1.3 mm continuum
evidence.quote: The data are deprojected using an inclination angle $i = 60\degree$ and a position angle $\phi = 346\degree$ (cite: MacGregor_2017).

what.value: Stellar mass of GQ Lup A 1.05 Msun

evidence.quote: using the mass of GQ Lup A, 1.05$M_{\odot}$ (cite: Wu_2017)

what.value: Gap width/depth to planet-mass-ratio fitting relations (Tables 1 and 2)

evidence.quote: we select related models from Tables 1 and 2 in (cite: Zhang_2018) to perform our subsequent calculations of planet-star mass ratios.

recipe.method: CASA reduction following Wu et al. 2017, three rounds phase-only self-cal, tclean natural weighting, recentred with fixvis

recipe.goal: Fit radial brightness profile in visibility domain
recipe.method: Deproject visibilities, fit Gaussians modulated by sinusoids to real visibilities via Hankel transform
key_parameters: i = 60 deg, PA = 346 deg, d = 152 pc; two Gaussians

recipe.goal: Identify and measure gaps and rings
recipe.method: Find local minima/maxima following Huang et al. 2018; plateau via normalized gradient > -0.05; depth by fitting function on either side
Convert disk mass to gas surface density, compute Stokes number, use Zhang et al. 2018 width and depth relations to get q, then planet mass
assumptions: gas-to-dust ratio 100; gamma = 0.1; max particle size 0.1 mm

answer_key.quantity: Integrated flux of GQ Lup A disk

evidence.quote: we retrieve an integrated flux of 26 mJy for the GQ Lup A disk
with an effective radius of 19 au as compared to the average DSHARP size of 50 au
The gap at 32 au (D2[^1]) has a width of 2.25 au and a depth of 0.957.
we present a mass range of 3.07-355 $M_{\Earth}$ for D1

not_stated_but_needed: Cleaning threshold, masks, image size and cell size
Flux calibrator and calibration details (taken from Wu et al. 2017)
Visibility binning used for the profile
Data/model details for the 3-Gaussian fit (parameters not tabulated)
Depth fitting function form for plateau feature
score_reason: Public data and simple model, but imaging, self-cal and 3-Gaussian fit details are unspecified.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, a visibility fit with a published model and numeric table results.
